title: Urban Traffic Flow Optimization Using Queueing Theory
summary: This paper addresses the optimization of urban traffic light timing at a major intersection using a combination of queueing theory and genetic algorithms.
keywords: traffic optimization; queueing theory; genetic algorithm; M/M/1 queue
problem_background: Urban traffic congestion has become a critical issue in modern cities. This study focuses on optimizing traffic light timing at a 4-way intersection to minimize average vehicle wait times.
problem_requirement: Given traffic flow data and intersection geometry, determine optimal traffic light timing parameters to minimize total delay.
problem_analysis: The problem requires modeling vehicle arrivals as stochastic processes, optimizing timing parameters, and validating with real-world data.

tasks.task_description: Model vehicle arrival patterns using Poisson distribution
tasks.task_analysis: Vehicle arrivals at the intersection follow a Poisson process. The arrival rate varies by time of day, with peak hours showing rates up to 60 vehicles per minute.
tasks.mathematical_modeling_process: We model the intersection as an M/M/1 queue where vehicles arrive according to Poisson process with rate lambda and service rate mu. The average wait time is W = 1/(mu - lambda).
tasks.solution_interpretation: The queueing model accurately predicts wait times under varying traffic conditions. The model performs best when arrival rates are below 85% of service capacity.
tasks.subtask_outcome_analysis: Model validation shows 92% accuracy in predicting wait times during off-peak hours.

tasks.task_description: Optimize traffic light timing using genetic algorithm
tasks.task_analysis: The optimization problem has multiple parameters: cycle length, green phase durations, and phase sequence. GA is suitable due to the complex solution space.
tasks.preliminary_formulas: Fitness function: f = 1 / (1 + total_delay), where total_delay = sum(wait_time for all vehicles)
tasks.mathematical_modeling_process: We encode timing parameters as chromosomes with real-valued genes. Selection uses tournament selection, crossover uses SBX operator. Mutation rate: 0.1, population size: 100.
tasks.execution_result: Optimal cycle: 90s, green phases: [30, 25, 20, 15] seconds, best fitness: 0.0042
tasks.solution_interpretation: GA converged after 150 generations. The solution reduces average wait time by 23% compared to fixed-timing baseline.
tasks.subtask_outcome_analysis: GA solution is robust across multiple random seeds, with fitness variance < 5%.

tasks.task_description: Validate model with real-world traffic data
tasks.task_analysis: Validation requires comparing model predictions with actual traffic measurements from sensors at the intersection.
tasks.preliminary_formulas: MAPE = (1/n) * sum(|actual - predicted| / actual), R^2 = 1 - SS_res / SS_tot
tasks.mathematical_modeling_process: We collected 24-hour traffic counts from loop detectors. Data was aggregated into 5-minute intervals and compared with model predictions.
tasks.solution_interpretation: The model shows good agreement with real traffic data, particularly during peak hours when traffic follows Poisson assumptions most closely.
tasks.subtask_outcome_analysis: Model performance is consistent across different days, indicating good generalization.
